assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology (incretin action, proglucagon processing, the active truncated peptide) led to long-acting agonists that transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with documented cardiovascular and renal benefit. Originality, clarity and breadth of impact are exceptional, and the physiology-to-therapy arc fits the prize well.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology and secretion of GLP-1) and Drucker (biology of GLP-1/GLP-2 and its therapeutic translation) are central; Mojsov's identification of the biologically active GLP-1(7-36) form is a strong third claim. Knudsen led liraglutide/semaglutide development and is an industry-translation candidate. Habener is not on the supplied list, which complicates a fair allocation. I am relying on memory of the priority disputes and have not verified them.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism has been confirmed for decades and clinical outcomes are confirmed by large independent trials. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue given the scale of use.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit among the original peptide-identification and therapeutic-development contributors is contested.
Long-term safety and durability of obesity effects are still being established, though this does not undermine the discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells with chimeric antigen receptors produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new therapeutic class. The concept is original and the clinical impact is clear and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (second-generation costimulatory CARs), June (clinical translation in CLL and ALL) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell therapy and early gene-engineered T cells) form a coherent trio. Credit from the Eshhar, Kuwana and Zelig Eshhar lineage is not in the supplied names, and I cannot verify how that would affect fairness.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and independent long-term follow-up confirm efficacy in hematologic cancers. Solid tumors, toxicity and access remain open, but the core discovery is mature.
uncertainties: First-generation CAR precursors by others are not in the credited names.
Limited efficacy in solid tumors suggests the field is still evolving.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Splice-switching antisense oligonucleotides correcting SMN2 exon 7 inclusion led to nusinersen, the first effective therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, which was a fatal infant motor neuron disease. As a motor-system neuroscientist I find the biological and clinical clarity compelling, and the work established a general antisense platform for neurological disease.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (mechanistic splicing work and the target identification) and Bennett (antisense chemistry and drug development at Ionis) are clear and compact. Other contributors such as Hua and Singh are not in the credited list, and the original SMN gene discovery by Melki and Lefebvre is a separate component.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with several years of independent real-world and trial evidence, and the platform has been replicated in other diseases. Timing is appropriate.
uncertainties: The SMN gene discovery (a distinct earlier contribution) is not credited here.
Intrathecal delivery limits and the relative role of competing gene therapy and small molecules.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics provided millisecond-precision, cell-type-specific control of neural activity, which transformed circuit neuroscience in my own area and many others. The impact on methods is exceptional and lasting. A methods prize is plausible, though the direct medical benefit is less than for therapeutic candidates.
assessment.attribution: Channelrhodopsin identification and characterization (Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg) and its deployment in neurons (Boyden, Deisseroth, and Miesenböck's earlier genetic approach) are all decisive. With six names a three-person limit forces a difficult choice, and my selection is one defensible configuration rather than a settled one.
assessment.maturity: Technique is confirmed in thousands of independent laboratories, with early clinical applications in vision restoration. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Six-way credit competition makes the three-person limit contentious.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: cGAS-STING defined how cytosolic DNA triggers innate immune responses, with relevance to infection, autoimmunity, interferonopathies and cancer immunity. The discovery of the second messenger cGAMP and its sensor cGAS is conceptually clear and original.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and cGAMP as the DNA sensor and second messenger, while Barber identified STING. Sun, Wu and Ishikawa are valid co-contributors, but Chen and Barber best capture the principal conceptual steps in my assessment. The role of other STING-pathway discoverers is uncertain to me.
assessment.maturity: Pathway is broadly confirmed and heavily reproduced. Therapeutic exploitation, for example STING agonists and antagonists, has not yet matured, so recognition rests on mechanism rather than medicine.
uncertainties: Clinical translation has so far been limited.
Priority split between sensor identification and adaptor identification may be disputed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR/mTOR is a master regulator of cell growth and metabolism linking nutrients to anabolic programs, with implications for cancer, aging, immunosuppression and metabolic disease. The discovery is fundamental and has lasting impact.
assessment.attribution: Hall discovered TOR genetically in yeast and framed its role in growth control. Schreiber's chemical genetic work on rapamycin targets is a decisive complementary contribution. Sabatini's mTORC1 nutrient-sensing work is important, but I judge the earliest steps to be more decisive. Brown, Sabatini and others are interdependent claims that I cannot fully resolve.
assessment.maturity: Highly confirmed, with rapalogs approved for transplantation and oncology. The field is mature and the recognition would be timely.
uncertainties: Credit among early rapamycin target discoverers (including those not in this list) is complex.
Therapeutic benefit of mTOR inhibition in aging is not established.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle HPV vaccines prevent infection and have sharply reduced cervical precancer and cancer, with strong public health consequences. The VLP concept is original and the outcome is unambiguous.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller developed L1 VLPs and Frazer (with Zhou) contributed to the early expression and VLP formation. Credit for the vaccine technology is shared and priority between groups has been contested, which I cannot resolve from memory. Zur Hausen's earlier recognition covered the viral cause of cervical cancer.
assessment.maturity: Long-term population-level effectiveness data are now strong and independent, so recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Priority among the VLP groups is disputed.
Prior prize to zur Hausen may be seen as covering part of this arc.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showing that TNF is a therapeutic target in rheumatoid arthritis established anti-cytokine therapy and changed treatment of several chronic inflammatory diseases. The translational story is clear and the impact is lasting.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini jointly demonstrated the TNF-driven cytokine cascade in rheumatoid synovium and led the first clinical trials of anti-TNF. This is a compact, defensible pair. Contributions from antibody engineers and other trial investigators are not credited, and I have not verified their relative roles.
assessment.maturity: Anti-TNF biologics have been used for more than two decades with extensive confirmation. Recognition is mature and possibly late relative to the 2003 Lasker recognition.
uncertainties: Biologic originators and other cytokine pioneers are outside the credited names.
The prize may be viewed as primarily translational rather than discovery-based.
